key_insight: Low-rank compression can preserve turbulent-flow statistics while substantially corrupting near-wall dissipation and nonlinear interscale energy transfer.
engineering_relevance: Modal energy-budget checks help set compression limits for large DNS databases when accurate turbulence physics matters more than fieldwise reconstruction alone.
method: Construct an extended space-time correlation operator roughly 100 times larger than snapshot POD's.
Extract its dominant range using a randomized range finder with communication-avoiding hierarchical QR.
Use a distributed, GPU-accelerated framework and validate reconstructions against statistics and modal energy budgets.
evidence_signal: Tests on compressor-cascade DNS with laminar and turbulent inflows show that aggressive compression preserves all one-point statistics within a few percent while producing roughly an order of magnitude larger errors in dissipation and interscale transfer.
watch_item: Do not select compression levels from retained energy or one-point statistics alone: high-order modes carry near-wall dissipation that these checks can miss.
paper_title: Compression of turbulent flow data through an extended space-time correlation: certification against the modal energy budget
